- When sentiment is negative (especially recent), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% to match true mean reversion.
- After sharp price spikes, model often overshoots downward in next period; reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid overcorrection.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for first 5–7 days.
- If sentiment is neutral or positive, model tends to overestimate; apply 1–2% downward bias to align with true mean.
- Model shows persistent lag in capturing sentiment shifts; if sentiment turns negative, delay forecast drop by 1–2 days and reduce slope.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture short-term volatility; add 0.5–1.0% volatility buffer if sentiment is volatile or recent.
